talks.title: Examining Access Control Vulnerabilities in GraphQL: A Feeld Case Study
talks.teaser: Examines authorization and access control vulnerabilities in GraphQL and REST APIs, using the Feeld dating app data leak as a case study in data exposure.
talks.summary:
API Access Control Mechanisms and Pitfalls

GraphQL provides flexible client-driven data querying across complex object graphs. However, decoupling query parsing from granular object-level authorization frequently introduces critical Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA) vulnerabilities.

Case Study: Feeld Dating App Vulnerability

Security review of the Feeld dating application revealed missing access control checks across GraphQL queries and associated REST endpoints. By manipulating user identifiers and object parameters in nested queries, unauthorized clients could retrieve private user data.

Impact on Sensitive Personal Media and Communications

The authorization bypass exposed sensitive personal records, including unencrypted photos, private videos, and confidential user messages. The flaw illustrates how schema complexity can obscure missing authorization checks at the field resolver level.

Remediation and Secure GraphQL Architecture

Preventing GraphQL authorization flaws requires implementing field-level authorization middleware, validating user ownership at the data resolver layer, and enforcing strict schema querying boundaries.
